candidates.original_title: The aging of the social mind-differential effects on components of social understanding
candidates.description: Age-related differences in empathy (sharing of a narrator's emotion) measured with the EmpaToM paradigm
candidates.citation_sentence: One exception is the study by Reiter et al. [62].
candidates.notes: Paper cites Reiter et al. as [62] but the actual Reiter et al. (2017) reference is [63] in the reference list; the original study is Reiter et al. (2017) with DOI 10.1038/s41598-017-10669-4. The replication found no significant age effect on empathy, consistent with the original's preservation finding, and the authors explicitly claim replication success. Paper cites Reiter et al. as [62] but the actual Reiter et al. paper is reference [63] in the reference list; reference [62] is Sze et al. (2012). The described original study (EmpaToM, empathy, compassion, ToM) matches Reiter et al. (2017). The replication found no significant age effect on empathy, consistent with the original's preservation finding.

candidates.original_title: The aging of the social mind-differential effects on components of social understanding
candidates.description: Age-related differences in Theory of Mind (reasoning about the narrator's thoughts) measured with the EmpaToM paradigm
candidates.citation_sentence: One exception is the study by Reiter et al. [62].
candidates.notes: Paper cites Reiter et al. as [62] but the actual Reiter et al. (2017) reference is [63] in the reference list. The replication replicated the ToM accuracy decline but did not replicate the ToM reaction time effect from the original. Paper cites Reiter et al. as [62] but the actual Reiter et al. paper is reference [63] in the reference list; reference [62] is Sze et al. (2012). The described original study matches Reiter et al. (2017). The replication found YA outperformed OA in ToM accuracy, consistent with the original's decline finding. The paper did not replicate the ToM reaction time interaction from the original.

candidates.original_title: The aging of the social mind—differential effects on components of social understanding
candidates.description: Older adults show preserved empathic responses relative to younger adults.
candidates.citation_sentence: Therefore, the object of this study was to replicate the effect of age on empathy, compassion and ToM found in the study of Reiter et al. [62] by using the same paradigm (EmpaToM) in a different setting (inside an MRI scanner) and in an independent sample of YA and OA but keeping all other methods as close as possible to the original study.

candidates.original_title: The aging of the social mind—differential effects on components of social understanding
candidates.description: Older adults show a decline in Theory of Mind performance relative to younger adults.
candidates.citation_sentence: Therefore, the object of this study was to replicate the effect of age on empathy, compassion and ToM found in the study of Reiter et al. [62] by using the same paradigm (EmpaToM) in a different setting (inside an MRI scanner) and in an independent sample of YA and OA but keeping all other methods as close as possible to the original study.
candidates.notes: The age-related decline in ToM accuracy was replicated, but the original age effect on ToM reaction time was not replicated; the authors describe the overall ToM replication as partial.
